title: Rotor V2 II · four-part plastic prototype
material: PLA Basic · grey, right nozzle external spool

snapshots.caption: Fresh pre-start camera view: whole installed bed visually clear, with known flat surface marks unchanged. No new parts or debris visible. This is clearance evidence before submission, not a during-print or completed-part image.

During accepted startup at 23:44:13 UTC: bed raised during automatic preparation; no printed objects or first-layer deposition yet. Existing flat surface marks remain visible. This is startup evidence, not a finished-part image or physical-fit check.

First deposition observed at 23:49:27 UTC: new curved perimeter and filled grey area visible behind the toolhead. No visible spaghetti or displaced object in the exposed region. The toolhead occludes part of the object; this does not verify all four first layers, whole-first-layer quality/completion or physical fit.

After-first-layer milestone at 00:07:14 UTC: four footprint regions correspond to the exact plate preview and remain in place. No visible loose spaghetti, displaced object or clearly lifted edge. Layer 2 telemetry establishes first-layer completion; toolhead occlusion, low angle and glare prevent whole-first-layer quality verification. Physical fit remains unverified.

Hourly view at 01:05:05 UTC, reported layer 9/242: four expected footprint regions remain in place. No visible loose spaghetti, displaced object or clearly lifted edge in exposed regions. Toolhead, low angle and glare conceal detail; whole-first-layer quality, physical fit and final print success remain unverified.

Recovered hourly camera at 02:04:28 UTC, reported layer 17/242: four objects remain in place and visibly build upward. No visible loose spaghetti, displaced object or clearly lifted edge in exposed regions. Toolhead, angle, glare and focus limit inspection. Whole-first-layer quality, physical fit and final success remain unverified.

Hourly view at 03:00:51 UTC, reported layer 24/242: four expected objects remain in place and visibly build upward. No visible loose spaghetti, displaced object or clearly lifted edge in exposed regions. Toolhead, angle, glare and focus conceal detail; whole-first-layer quality, physical fit and final success remain unverified.

Hourly view at 03:55:43 UTC, reported layer 31/242: front body and rear-left ratchet region clearly visible, continuing to build in place. Toolhead occludes the other regions and part of the body; all four objects are not established by this frame. No visible anomaly in exposed regions. Angle, glare and focus limit inspection; whole-layer quality and physical fit remain unverified.

Hourly view at 04:51:39 UTC, reported layer 39/242: all four footprint regions visible and continuing to build; front body top surface and raised central features are visible. No loose spaghetti, displaced object or clearly lifted edge visible in exposed regions. Toolhead partly limits rear-left detail; angle, glare and focus conceal detail. No whole-layer, fit, strength or final-quality acceptance.

Hourly view at 05:47:46 UTC, reported layer 93/242: front body and rear-right cassette clearly visible with taller features; rear-left ratchet partly visible. Narrow rear arm region and some left detail are hidden by the toolhead, so all four regions are not established. No visible anomaly in exposed regions; angle, glare and focus limit detail. No whole-layer, fit, strength or terminal-quality acceptance.

Terminal camera at 06:41:35 UTC after printer-reported FINISH: all four expected part regions visible on the occupied bed, front body lower edge cropped. No obvious displaced object, major spaghetti or clearly lifted edge visible in exposed regions. Thin strands inside one front bore and support details require physical cleanup inspection. No whole-part, cleanup, fit, strength, assembly or electrical-operation acceptance; bed remains uncleared.

notes: Printer-reported completion was first observed at 2026-10-23T06:40:34Z: exact accepted job FINISH, 100%, layer 242/242, no skipped objects, print error 0 and no HMS entries. Last RUNNING was observed at 06:38:33 UTC, 99%, layer 235/242. Exact actual finish time, duration seconds and filament usage remain unknown; finishedAt, actualSeconds and actualGrams stay null. Device-reported elapsed 417 minutes is rounded telemetry only, separate from the 23555-second / 58.19g slicer estimates. At first terminal observation the bed measured 52°C with target 0°C; independent read-only telemetry during the 06:41:35 camera capture confirmed FINISH with bed 50°C/0°C. The approved final image shows four expected part regions on the occupied bed, with the front body lower edge cropped. No obvious displaced object, major spaghetti or clearly lifted edge is visible in exposed regions. Thin strands are visible inside one front bore; support details and cleanup require physical inspection. Removal, whole-part quality, cleanup, fit, strength, assembly and electrical operation are unverified. Bed clearance and successor start remain held; rotor III is not authorized to start by this record. Original acceptance-observation timestamp, exact file/plate identity, historical visibility limits, missing evidence and camera recovery remain preserved. Earlier recorded observations: Printer acceptance was observed at 2026-10-22T23:42:25.190Z (01:42 on 23 October in Oslo). startedAt preserves that observation/receipt timestamp, not a measured deposition-onset time. First observed RUNNING stage was Cooling chamber, about 392 minutes remaining, print error 0 and no HMS entries. The initial startup observations preceded visible deposition; whole-first-layer quality and adhesion remain unverified; this is acceptance and startup evidence, not completed-quality evidence. The human explicitly authorized this ONE rotor II prototype despite rotor I not yet assembled, saying they were in bed and to PRINT THE NEXT ONE. Physical fit and rotor-I assembly acceptance remain unverified; the explicit sequence exception permits proceeding before that check and does not establish quality or function. Four new rotor II parts reuse the existing numbered ring II; no new numbered ring is printed. The blank cassette is non-electrical. Grey PLA on the right nozzle normal external spool; textured plate, bed leveling and flow calibration enabled, AMS and timelapse disabled. Four walls, 30% gyroid, 0.10 mm layers / 0.20 mm first layer, 8 mm outer brim and normal supports. Support removal, fine features, captive hardware, dimensional fit, retention, strength, ring-arm action and full assembly/operation remain unverified. Completed rotor-I combined run 27cd remains separate. Actual finish time, duration and filament usage are unknown. A fresh startup camera at 23:44:13 UTC shows the bed raised during automatic preparation, with no printed objects yet. Subsequent root-reported startup telemetry remained RUNNING / Cleaning nozzle tip, bed 55°C with target 55°C, right nozzle 241°C with target 240°C, print error 0 and no HMS entries. First-layer deposition was subsequently observed in a fresh 23:49:27 UTC camera view: a new curved perimeter and filled grey patch are visible behind the toolhead. No spaghetti or displaced object is visible in the exposed region, but the toolhead occludes part of the object; all four first layers are not yet visible or complete. Fresh same-job telemetry reported RUNNING, 1%, layer 1/242, elapsed 7 minutes and approximately 386 minutes remaining, error 0 and no HMS entries, right nozzle 220°C/220°C and bed 55°C/55°C. The telemetry elapsed field is not a measured total print duration. At that early first-deposition observation, whole-first-layer quality/completion, physical fit and final print quality remained unverified. At 00:07:14 UTC on 23 October, a fresh image compared with the exact slice preview showed all four expected footprint regions: scalloped body at front, cassette rear-right, ratchet rear-left partly under the moving head, and thin arm at the back. No loose spaghetti, displaced object or clearly lifted edge was visible. The print had reached layer 2/242, so first-layer completion is established by telemetry; whole-first-layer quality remains unverified because the toolhead, glare and low angle hide detail. Latest subscribe-only telemetry reported RUNNING at 6%, approximately 368 minutes remaining, no errors/HMS and bed 55°C/55°C; the 00:07:03 MCP observation reported elapsed 24 minutes and right nozzle 220°C/220°C. Reported elapsed and remaining time are not a measured total duration. Physical fit and final print success remain unverified. Hourly monitoring at 01:05 UTC: fresh MCP and independent subscribe-only telemetry agreed RUNNING, 19%, layer 9/242, about 315 device-estimated minutes remaining, bed 55°C/55°C, right nozzle 220°C/220°C, error 0, no HMS entries and no skipped objects. The 01:05:05 camera shows all four expected footprint regions still in place with no visible loose spaghetti, displaced object or clearly lifted edge in exposed regions. Toolhead occlusion, glare and low angle limit inspection. Whole-first-layer quality, physical fit and final print success remain unverified; reported elapsed 83 minutes is not a measured total duration. Four objects remain in their footprint regions and are visibly building upward, with no visible loose spaghetti, displacement or clearly lifted edge in exposed regions. Toolhead occlusion, low angle, glare and focus limit inspection. MCP estimated 205 minutes remaining, while an independent adjacent read estimated 204 minutes; both remain device estimates. The four expected objects remain positioned and visibly build upward, with no visible loose spaghetti, displaced object or clearly lifted edge in exposed regions. Toolhead occlusion, low angle, glare and focus limit inspection. Hourly camera milestone at 03:55–03:56 UTC: fresh MCP and independent subscribe-only telemetry confirmed the same job RUNNING, 61%, layer 31/242, about 150 device-estimated minutes remaining, bed 55°C/55°C, error 0 and no HMS entries or skipped objects. This frame clearly shows only the front body and rear-left ratchet region continuing to build in place. The toolhead substantially occludes the rear-right and narrow rear regions and part of the body, so this frame does not establish all four objects. No loose spaghetti, displaced object or clearly lifted edge is visible in exposed regions. Angle, glare and focus further limit inspection. Whole-first-layer quality, physical fit and final success remain unverified; reported elapsed 253 minutes is not a measured total duration. Hourly camera milestone at 04:51–04:52 UTC: the same job remained RUNNING, 75%, layer 39/242, with no faults or skipped objects and bed 55°C/55°C. MCP estimated 97 minutes remaining and independent adjacent telemetry estimated 96 minutes; both are device estimates. All four footprint regions are visible in this new frame, with continued build-up and the front body top surface and raised central features visible. No loose spaghetti, displaced object or clearly lifted edge is visible in exposed regions. Toolhead partly limits rear-left detail; low angle, glare and focus further limit inspection. This new visibility does not change the prior 03:55 frame’s two-region occlusion limit or establish whole-layer quality, physical fit, strength or final print success. The front body and rear-right cassette are clearly visible with taller walls/features, while the rear-left ratchet is partly visible. The toolhead obscures the narrow rear arm region and some left detail; this frame does not establish all four regions. No loose spaghetti, displaced object or clearly lifted edge is visible in exposed regions. Low angle, glare and focus limit detail.
